environment.description: Same Kubernetes deployment but with a content-integrity sidecar (Notary v2 / cosign-based admission). All scripts in /opt/etl/scripts are mounted from a read-only ConfigMap whose SHA-384 digests are pinned in the pod spec annotation 'integrity.k8s.io/script-digests'. The sidecar intercepts exec syscalls via a seccomp-bpf profile (custom notify filter on execve/execveat) and validates that any file passed to sh -c has its content hash matching the pinned digest set before allowing execution. Additionally, the Kafka consumer sidecar proxy (Envoy with ext_authz) validates message payloads against a strict regex allowlist (^[a-z_]+\.sh\|[a-zA-Z0-9 ,._-]*$) before forwarding to the application port, rejecting any message containing shell metacharacters (;|&|`|$|>|<|\(|\)) in the params field. The combination of content-hash verification on executed scripts (analogous to SRI for web resources) and input sanitization at the proxy layer prevents both script tampering and parameter injection.
